in_text_mentions: , about 41 mm × 29 mm × 53 mm in size, with clear boundary, and multiple linear partitions were seen in it. Intrahepatic bile duct dilatation was also found. On contrast enhanced CT scans, the capsule and septum enhanced, but no enhancement was found inside the tumor. The medial side of the tumor was adjacent to the main portal vein, and the portal vein ran normally, with local compression of the right branch changing (Figure 2). Subcutaneous edema was found in bilateral iliolumbar, lower abdominal wall and proximal thigh. Spleen, kidney and pancreas were normal. The mass was diagnosed as MHL.

in_text_mentions: s showed expected mild elevations in AST (58 U/L) and ALT (43 U/L), and alkaline phosphatase and total bilirubin remained within acceptable ranges. The patient met the criteria for discharge at this time and was sent home with her parents. A follow-up appointment two weeks later was uneventful with no pain, fever, swelling, redness, or drainage from the well-healing incisions. The pathology report of the solid tumor specimen reaffirmed the preoperative (core biopsy) diagnosis of mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver (Figure 6). The patient remained recurrence-free at follow-up three months later.

plate_findings.evidence: Mode ultrasound section showed right hepatic lesion, segment VI with many echogenic septae inside

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is a mode ultrasound section showing a hepatic lesion characterized by numerous echogenic septae, consistent with the diagnosis of mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver. B: Panel B shows the mode ultrasound view of the hepatic lesion, demonstrating the overall structure which is consistent with the described mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver. C: Panel C shows Doppler ultrasound emphasizing the solid content and associated vasculature within the hepatic lesion, supporting the heterogeneous nature of the mesenchymal hamartoma. D: Panel D shows real-time 2D shearwave elastography, providing quantitative stiffness data (low stiffness) for the solid components of the hepatic lesion, consistent with mesenchymal hamartoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: A panel showing the primary hepatic mass on T2W MRI, consistent with the case description of a complex lesion. B: Coronal view of the hepatic mass, confirming its presence and extent. C: Shows the low signal characteristics of the mass on T1-weighted imaging. D: Demonstrates the dynamic enhancement pattern (peripheral enhancement) characteristic of MHL on MRI. E: Shows dynamic progression of contrast within the mass, suggesting a septated or loculated structure. F: Shows late dynamic enhancement pattern, characteristic of the mass's internal architecture.
panels.attribution_text: Le et al. Infantile mesenchymal hamartoma of the liver with elevated alpha fetoprotein.. BJR case reports 2021. doi:10.1259/bjrcr.20200196. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced MRI detected a right hepatic lesion in the segment VI. (a and b) The lesion had heterogeneous high signal intensity in axial and coronal T2W. c: The lesion has heterogeneous low signal intensity in T1W and T1 pre gadolinium. d: Heterogeneous gadolinium contrast opacification, peripheral enhancement of the arterial phase. (e and f) Contrast opacification progressive centripetally in the venous phase (T1 portal venous phase) and late phase (T1 delay phase) and without filling the whole lesion.
in_text_mentions: Contrast-enhanced MRI detected a right hepatic lesion in the segment VI, measuring 56 × 53 mm. The lesion had heterogeneous high signal intensity to the liver parenchyma in T2W, heterogeneous low signal intensity in T1W, heterogeneous gadolinium contrast opacification, peripheral enhancement of the arterial phase, progressive centripetally in the venous phase and late phase without filling the whole lesion. Delayed phase was taken through dynamic T1WI vibe pulse with contrast agent, which was recorded after 5–7 min from beginning of artery phase. (Figure 2).
